newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MALAYSIA JULY PALM OIL OUTPUT SEEN UP SIX PCT.
newsitem.headline: MALAYSIA JULY PALM OIL OUTPUT SEEN UP SIX PCT.

text.p: Malaysia's crude palm oil output in July is estimated to have risen by up to six percent over June's 787,807 tonnes, a Reuters survey of six local plantation houses on Wednesday found.
The Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) is scheduled to release official July output/stock/export data on August 15.

"It is a seasonal factor. The rise was mainly from Peninsular Malaysia," a plantation company official said. "Over in East Malaysia, production is tapering off because of lack of rains which has affected the ripening of fruits."
Private crop forecaster Ivan Wong had earlier projected July output at 823,000 tonnes. Wong is due to release his latest crop report on Thursday.
Traders have estimated end-July stocks at 800,000-810,000 tonnes against PORLA's 786,123 tonnes at end-June.
Exports in July were estimated at 700,000-710,000 tonnes against 612,124 tonnes in June.
